    About

    Women are not merely defined by their struggles. They are recognised for their humour, contradictions, relationships and capacity to shape their own lives.

    About

    A scholar of context

    Researcher, writer, coach and mediator. Based in Chicago, working between India and the United States.

    I study women's lives in the places they actually happen: neighbourhoods, kitchens, classrooms, offices and the long distances between countries. My research asks who gets to decide, and how women negotiate that question inside family, culture and work.

    That question also shapes my plays, my Hindi poetry and my novel. Across all of it, I try to show women with their humour, intelligence and contradictions intact, rather than as figures of suffering. I also coach, mediate and teach, because ideas about agency should be useful in a room.

    Research philosophy

    Three pillars

    Culture and context

    Women's choices only make sense inside the cultures, families and economies that frame them.

    Identity and agency

    Identity is plural and shifting, and agency shows up in small negotiations as well as big decisions.

    Bridging North and South

    Research that moves between India, the United States and the wider Global South, in both directions.

    Stories and workshops

    Stories that build agency

    Plays, Hindi poetry and a novel about the humour and resilience of women, and the workshops that carry the same ideas into classrooms and workplaces.

    Plays

    The plays

    Marriage Mirage (2020) is a social comedy about three women from different generations, Munni, Mangala and Maggie, whose romantic lives become unexpectedly intertwined. Set against Indian middle-class sensibilities, it uses satire to look at marriage, commitment and the surprising ways women negotiate their relationships.

    My Frustrated Lady (2021) follows a newly immigrated Indian woman and her encounters with a Caucasian couple. The play looks at elitism, subtle racism and cultural misunderstanding in urban America, and at the emotional wellbeing of South Asian women in the diaspora.

    Hindi poetry

    मोहब्बत में मय से माँ तक

    Written in Hindi with Hindi-Urdu literary influences, the collection turns to love, motherhood, memory and the emotional worlds of women. Where the plays are lively and satirical, the poems make room for intimacy and reflection.

    Novel · 2020 · The Making of Indian Womanhood

    The novel

    Red Chilli Pickle & Moonlit Terraces

    The title pairs two familiar images: the sensory richness of food and domestic tradition, and the openness of a moonlit terrace. Together they suggest the many spaces where women's lives, relationships and identities unfold.

    The novel follows the everyday experiences that shape womanhood: family, social expectation, cultural belonging, and the ways women come to understand themselves and the world around them.

    Digital projects

    Ancient wisdom, modern lives

    Digital experiences for intuition, reflection and mind, body and spirit connection. Built as tools for questioning, not prediction.

    Tarot-e-Taal

    Three decks, one journey

    Tarot, the symbolic language of cards, meets taal, the rhythm of life. Choose a deck, choose a card or spread, and read it against your own circumstances.

    Deck 01

    The Universe

    What is happening around me, and what larger possibilities can I explore?

    For broader perspective, timing, change and the links between choices and circumstance.

    Deck 02

    Plan It

    What choices can I make, and how might I move forward?

    For decisions and goals. It helps you see your own agency rather than deciding for you.

    Deck 03

    Energy

    What am I experiencing within myself, and what needs my attention?

    For emotional, mental, physical and spiritual check-ins, alongside meditation and journaling.

    Energy Check

    Energy Check

    Symbolic cards, journaling prompts and a meditation calendar, for personal use and for coaches, healers and mental health professionals.

    Pause, listen, reflect, and reconnect with the wisdom within.
